formula: party ~ income + ideo + (1 | state)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: ROS Pew example (pew.R) describes party identification by income and ideology and summarises by state (as.numeric(pew_pre$state)); it fits no model, so the response is the reader's. Respondents in state (50 + DC), rendered (1 | state) as an exhaustive set of many areas (#162). Response party (republican/democrat/independent/no-preference/other, filed categorical); income and ideo are ordered Stata factors. rid respondent id and survey weight ignored. Outside check: stands.

formula: Surv(time, censor) ~ late * treat + (1 | id)
notes: Diabetic-retinopathy trial: two eyes (eye) per patient (id), one of them treated (treat); late marks late-onset diabetes, type a copy of it. The publisher's solution to MLMUS4 exercise 15.6 (ex15_6_blindness.do) splits time at 16 cut points and fits xtpoisson _d p1-p16 late treat late_treat, exposure(length) normal by id: a piecewise-exponential model with a lognormal patient frailty; its part 4 tests treat by interval. Exercise 14.6 fits the same terms on the discrete time scale (discrete) by melogit on the expanded data. Survival: time continuous, censor in ignore, Surv() in the formula (catheter, m3#24); the piecewise-exponential family is outside Family. Outside check: the solution's model replaces the proposal.

formula: h ~ male + (1 | pair) + (1 | pair:ifelse(M == 1, pair, member)), weighted by freq
notes: Hay fever in 3,807 twin pairs (Hopper et al. 1990), stored as 20 pair patterns of two members, each with a pair-level frequency weight freq. The publisher's solution to MLMUS4 exercise 16.11 (ex16_11_twinhay.do) fits the ADE model meprobit h male || pair:, fweight(freq) || k:, with k = pair for monozygotic (M == 1) and member for dizygotic pairs, and derives the additive and dominance variances; Rabe-Hesketh's 2010 German Stata Users talk (pp. 19-21) fits it by gllamm, then the AE model constraining the two variances equal. The k level is a unit no column holds, so it stays in the formula only. Outside check: the solution's model replaces the inferred one.

formula: Surv(start, stop, infection) ~ treat + (1 | center) + (1 | id:number), a Poisson model of the risk sets with an orthogonal quartic baseline in time
notes: Randomized trial of infection prevention (treat) in 13 centers: 128 patients (id) with up to 8 episodes (number), each row an episode from start to stop ending in an infection or censoring; 694 of the 897 rows are padding with start == stop. The publisher's solution to MLMUS4 exercise 16.9 (ex16_9_infections.do) drops them, splits the episodes at the failure times and fits mepoisson _d t1-t4 treat, exposure(length) || center: || idnum: with idnum = group(id number), center and episode frailties, tested against the episode frailty alone by lrtest; exercises 15.7 and 15.8 fit Cox models with standard errors clustered by id. Each episode is one row, an observation-level effect, so id and number are in ignore. Survival: stop continuous, infection in ignore, Surv() in the formula (catheter, m3#24). Outside check: the solution's model replaces the proposal; sex, age, steroids and propulac are unused usable columns.

formula: pmax(numpos, 2) ~ religion + year + age + gender + (1 | respond), cumulative logit
notes: Hand pass #82: MLMUS4 exercise 11.5 (ex11_5_abortion.do) fits meologit score i.religion i.year age male || person: after recode score 0/2=2; score, person and male are numpos, respond and gender here. Part 3d refits it with standard errors clustered on district, which gets no random effect. The merge of scores 0-2 lives in the formula only, so the row keeps all eight levels. The CMM software review fits a respondent-intercept ordered logit with religion only; Goldstein (1995, section 3.2) fits a three-level Normal model to normal scores. Outside check: the review's section 4.1 fits numpos and names party preference among the covariates, so this row is model 1 and party files no row.

formula: length ~ nonlinear exponential curve a + b*exp(-conc/th) in conc; common th, correlated Strip effects on a and b
notes: NONLINEAR: Muscle.Rd (Baumann and Waldvogel 1963): shortening (length) of 21 heart-muscle strips (Strip) of rats over CaCl2 concentration (conc). Venables's S workshop slides (slide 75; not read here, the page is restricted) fit the nonlinear mixed model with Strip effects on a and b; MASS's scripts/ch08.R fits the same curve to its copy muscle as nls(log(Length) ~ alpha[Strip] + beta*rho^Conc) with fixed strip intercepts, Conc in multiples of 2.2 mM. Pinheiro and Bates (2000) fit no model to these data. Outside check: the formula in words.

formula: weight ~ nonlinear SSlogis growth in Time; Asym fixed by Year*Variety, xmid by Year + Variety, scal by Year; Plot effects on Asym; residual variance a power of the fitted value
notes: NONLINEAR: Soybean.Rd (App. A.27; Davidian and Giltinan 1995, sec. 1.1.3): leaf weight of 48 plots (Plot) over days after planting (Time), two varieties in three years. Pinheiro and Bates (2000, sec. 6.3; nlme's scripts/ch06.R) fit nlsList(SSlogis) per Plot, fm1Soy.nlme with Plot effects on all three parameters, fm2 with varPower, fm3 with each parameter fixed by Year, and last fm4Soy.nlme with the parameter models above and a Plot effect on Asym alone (pp. 293-295). Outside check: fm4 replaces the recalled model.

formula: uptake ~ nonlinear SSasympOff curve in conc; Asym and lrc fixed by Type*Treatment, common c0; Plant effects on Asym
notes: NONLINEAR: re-export of base R's CO2, uptake of 12 plants (Plant) of two types, chilled or not, over ambient CO2 concentration (conc). Pinheiro and Bates (2000, sec. 8.2; nlme's scripts/ch08.R) fit nlsList(SSasympOff) per plant, fm1CO2.nlme with Plant effects on Asym, lrc and c0, fm2 on Asym and lrc, fm3 and fm4 with Asym, then lrc too, fixed by Type*Treatment, and last fm5CO2.nlme with a Plant effect on Asym alone, compared with an nls fit. conc is the nonlinear input, a covariate. Outside check: fm5 replaces the recalled model.

formula: circumference ~ SSlogis(age, Asym, xmid, scal), tree-specific Asym (logistic growth)
notes: NONLINEAR: logistic growth curve (SSlogis) of trunk circumference in age, tree-specific asymptote. Help page fits nlmer(circumference ~ SSlogis(age) ~ Asym|Tree) in a dontrun block; Pinheiro & Bates 2000. Tree is the grouping. Second reading #22: age is the nonlinear input, a covariate. Outside check: stands; Pinheiro and Bates (2000, sec. 8.2; nlme's scripts/ch08.R) fit fm1Oran.nlme with Tree effects on all three parameters and keep fm2Oran.nlme, Tree effects on Asym alone, by anova.

formula: conc ~ SSfol first-order absorption/elimination oral PK model (Dose, Time); common lKe, uncorrelated Subject effects on lKa and lCl
notes: NONLINEAR: SSfol first-order absorption and elimination oral PK model in Dose and Time (MEMSS calls it a two-compartment open model); the help page fits nls(conc ~ SSfol(Dose, Time)) per subject and cites Davidian & Giltinan 1995 sections 5.5/6.6 and P&B A.29. Pinheiro and Bates (2000, sec. 8.2; nlme's scripts/ch08.R) fit fm1Theo.nlme with correlated Subject effects on lKe, lKa and lCl, fm2 with uncorrelated ones and last fm3Theo.nlme without the lKe effect, compared by anova and checked by its plots; a variance-function fit fm4 is commented out. All rows are measured. Spot check #22: Dose and Time are the covariates; Wt stays an unused column. Outside check: fm3 replaces the first fit.

formula: category ~ male*female + (1|block:male:female), weighted by count
notes: Jansen (1990) ordinal extravariation model; the help page fits no mixed model. Rows are cells of a contingency table (block x cross x category) with the number of plants in count, so the ordinal response is weighted by count (count in ignore as a weight) and each male-by-female cross defines a population, hence male*female fixed; the plot block:male:female is the random level. The measurer counts cells, not plants, as observations (adjudication #22). Outside check: the 48 block-by-cross plots and the count-weighted ordinal response stand; Jansen's (1990) article was not read, so the male*female fixed part stays unverified.

formula: weight ~ Diet * poly(Time, 2) + (0 + Time | Chick), with AR(1) residuals within Chick
notes: Body weight of 50 chicks (Chick) on four protein diets (Diet) over 21 days (ChickWeight.Rd; Crowder and Hand 1990). Gurarie et al.'s Techniques and Concepts in Movement Ecology (ch. 10, Mixed models) fit lme(weight ~ Diet * poly(Time, 2), random = ~ (Time - 1) | Chick) and compare it by AICc with a fit without the Diet by time terms, each also with corAR1 residuals; Diet * poly(Time, 2) with AR(1) residuals wins. The quadratic stays in the formula only, Time named once; the contract adds a random intercept. The help page fits no mixed model, and SSlogis's example fits one chick. Outside check: the tutorial's linear model replaces the proposed logistic growth curve, so the row is no longer nonlinear.

formula: density ~ logistic assay calibration curve (SSlogis) in log(conc); run-specific parameters
notes: NONLINEAR: ELISA of recombinant DNase in rat serum, optical density (density) over known concentrations (conc) in 11 assay runs (Run; DNase.Rd; Davidian and Giltinan 1995, sec. 5.2.4, not read here). The help page fits nls(SSlogis) and nls(SSfpl) in log(conc) to run 1 alone; an r-help reply (Pikal, 2007) fits nlme on nlsList(SSfpl), a Q&A answer and no published model. The logistic calibration curve with Run effects is the reader's. conc is the nonlinear input. Outside check: published_model no.

formula: 2-parameter logistic IRT (hier_2pl); crossed person (jj) and item (ii); binary correctness from item discrimination times (ability minus difficulty), item parameters from an estimated bivariate population
documented_prior: theta ~ normal(0, 1); L_Omega ~ lkj_corr_cholesky(4); mu[1] ~ normal(0, 1); mu[2] ~ normal(0, 5); tau[1] ~ exponential(.1); tau[2] ~ exponential(.1)
notes: NONLINEAR: rendered from Stan (hier_2pl); grade-12 science assessment (Wood et al. 2003, mirt). Crossed person (jj) x item (ii) binary responses; nonlinear in the random effects (discrimination x ability), so no lme4 form; a 1PL/Rasch reading would be y ~ (1|jj) + (1|ii). RULE GAP: posteriordb IRT posteriors are nonlinear 2PL/GPCM; filed under the NONLINEAR rule with person and item as grouping factors. Outside check: stands.

formula: generalized rating-scale IRT (grsm_latent_reg_irt): adjacent-category logits alpha[ii]*theta[jj] - beta[ii] - kappa[category], crossed person (jj) and item (ii); item discriminations and locations with fixed prior scales, locations and steps summing to zero
documented_prior: alpha ~ lognormal(1, 1); beta ~ normal(0, 3); kappa ~ normal(0, 3); lambda_adj ~ student_t(3, 0, 1); theta ~ normal(W_adj * lambda_adj, 1)
notes: NONLINEAR: rendered from Stan (grsm_latent_reg_irt); 1992 Euro-Barometer science attitudes (ltm Science data). Ordinal responses (4 categories). The discrimination alpha multiplies the ability theta, so no lme4 form; theta ~ normal(W_adj * lambda_adj, 1), W holding only an intercept. Outside check: a generalized rating-scale model, not a graded one.

formula: choice ~ categorical softmax over four brands with shared disp, feat and price coefficients; fixed sunshine, keebler and nabisco intercepts and a zero private intercept; independent personId effects for sunshine, keebler and nabisco, nabisco's shared by private, each Normal(0, 0.1) with its scale fixed
documented_prior: beta_feat, beta_disp, beta_price ~ Normal(0, 1); alpha[alt] ~ Normal(0, 1); beta_individual[person, alt] ~ Normal(0, 0.1)
notes: PyMC generalized_linear_models/GLM-discrete-choice_models.myst.md fits a repeat-choice (mixed/conditional logit) model over cracker brands with an individual-specific intercept per personId (factorize(personId)). RULE GAP: discrete-choice model with alternative-specific attributes (display/feature/price per brand) as covariates and the chosen brand as the categorical response, rendered with a person random intercept. lastChoice is the previous-occasion choice (alternate); personChoiceId/choiceId are row ids. Code read #15: model_4 draws beta_individual[person, alt] ~ Normal(0, 0.1), a fixed, not estimated, scale, independent per alternative, examples/generalized_linear_models/GLM-discrete-choice_models.myst.md:569; utilities u0-u3 and softmax, examples/generalized_linear_models/GLM-discrete-choice_models.myst.md:571-601. The code's private utility has intercept 0 (alpha[private] is declared but unused) and reuses nabisco's person effect beta_individual[person, 2], examples/generalized_linear_models/GLM-discrete-choice_models.myst.md:589-593, so three person effects enter. Outside check: the formula states model_4's utilities.

formula: I(decision %in% c("CC", "IC")) ~ 1 + (1 | disadvantaged) + (1 | committing), bernoulli(logit): foul_called = 1 for CC/IC, 0 for CNC/INC
documented_prior: mu_theta ~ Normal(0, 100); sigma_theta ~ HalfCauchy(2.5); sigma_b ~ HalfCauchy(2.5); Delta_theta ~ Normal(0, 1); Delta_b ~ Normal(0, 1)
notes: PyMC case_studies/item_response_nba.myst.md fits a Bayesian IRT/Rasch model to NBA foul calls: crossed player random effects theta (disadvantaged) and b (committing) with hierarchical hyperpriors. RULE GAP: the modelled outcome is a binary foul_called recoded from decision (CC/IC = foul, CNC/INC = no foul); the loaded table only carries decision (4 categories), filed as the categorical response with the binary recode noted. committing_position/disadvantaged_position are unused covariates (an extra hierarchical layer left as an exercise). Code read #15: the model is pm.Bernoulli(logit_p = theta[disadvantaged] - b[committing]) on foul_called, the binary recode of decision (CC/IC = 1), examples/case_studies/item_response_nba.myst.md:120-131, 198-217; theta carries the intercept mu_theta; foul_called is not a column of the table, so response stays decision (a recoded response names its raw column) and the formula states the recode. Outside check: stands.

formula: log(earn) ~ height + (1 + height || eth)
documented_prior: mu_a1 ~ normal(0, 1); mu_a2 ~ normal(0, 1); a1 ~ normal(10*mu_a1, sigma_a1); a2 ~ normal(0.01*mu_a2, sigma_a2); sigma_a1, sigma_a2, sigma_y ~ cauchy(0, 5)
notes: ARM Ch.13 earnings varying-slope model (README earnings_vary_si: lmer(log(earn) ~ 1 + (1 + height | eth))); no own earnings.stan. The Latin-square model of section 13.5 is model 2. y is the adjusted response and x duplicates height, both ignored. Code read #15: a1 ~ normal(10 * mu_a1, sigma_a1); a2 ~ normal(0.01 * mu_a2, sigma_a2) drawn independently (earnings_vary_si.stan:31-32), so ||; the slope mean is the fixed height effect, as in the script's M1 <- lmer (y ~ x + (1 + x | eth.ok)) (13.4_UnderstandingCorrelationsBetweenIntercepts&Slopes.R:38); the first fit passes earn + 1 (:39). Outside check: stands.

formula: Surv(month, left) ~ sentiment + level + strata(gender) + (1 | field), shared gamma frailty by field
documented_prior: lambda0[interval, gender] ~ Gamma(0.01, 0.01); sigma_frailty ~ Normal(46.23, 1); mu_frailty ~ Normal(44.91, 1); frailty[field] ~ Gamma(mu_frailty, sigma_frailty); beta[pred] ~ Normal(0, 1)
notes: PyMC survival_analysis/frailty_models.myst.md fits a Cox-PH shared-frailty survival model with a gamma group frailty across field. RULE GAP: survival time month is the censored response (left = event/censoring indicator, ignored, per the census survival rule); the shared frailty over field is the grouping factor so field is not also a fixed covariate; the individual-frailty variant is observation-level and not a grouping factor. Spot check verdict (Alex, 2026-10-07, #24): survival response (month, left), left part of the response in the formula and in ignore per the census kidney convention; gender stratifies the baseline hazard; intention is not in the model. Outside check: stands; McNulty's Handbook of Regression Modeling in People Analytics (sec. 10.3) fits a frailty Cox model on the same table with gender as a covariate.

formula: NMOVES ~ 1 + 19/(1 + xmid*exp(-scal10*GAME - scal01*READ - scal11*READ*GAME + u)), logistic growth between 1 and 20 moves; correlated ID effects on scal10 and u
notes: NONLINEAR: 17 children (ID) play up to 27 games of fox and geese (GAME), NMOVES the moves per game, READ their reading level. Singer and Willett (2003, Table 6.6; UCLA's R code for ch. 6) fit model A, nlme(nmoves ~ 1 + 19/(1 + xmid*exp(-scal*game + u)), fixed = scal + xmid ~ 1, random = scal + u ~ 1 | id), then last model B with READ and its interaction with GAME in the exponent, random = scal10 + u ~ 1 | id, plotted by reading level (Fig. 6.10). Outside check: model B replaces the mix of the two.

formula: Height (cm) ~ a linear intercept plus exp of a cubic in I(Age (yr) - 8); correlated Individual effects on the exponent's intercept and linear age term
notes: NONLINEAR: Goldstein (1995, Multilevel Statistical Models, sec. 5.5, eq. 5.18, Table 5.14): 577 heights of 197 French Canadian boys aged 5 to 10 (Demirjian et al. 1982), fitted by the Jenss-Bayley-type curve y = exp(b0 + b1 t + b2 t^2 + b3 t^3 + u0 + u1 t) + a0 + e, t the age about 8 years. Outside check: stands, the formula stated.

formula: log(earn) ~ I(height - mean(height)) + (1 + I(height - mean(height)) || eth) + (1 + I(height - mean(height)) || age) + (1 + I(height - mean(height)) || eth:age)
documented_prior: mu_a1, mu_a2, mu_b1, mu_b2, mu_c, mu_d ~ normal(0, 1); a1 ~ normal(10*mu_a1, sigma_a1); a2 ~ normal(mu_a2, sigma_a2); b1 ~ normal(10*mu_b1, sigma_b1); b2 ~ normal(0.1*mu_b2, sigma_b2); c ~ normal(10*mu_c, sigma_c); d ~ normal(0.1*mu_d, sigma_d); sigma_a1, sigma_a2, sigma_b1, sigma_b2, sigma_c, sigma_d, sigma_y bounded to (0, 100) without a sampling statement
notes: ARM sec. 13.5 Latin-square model of log earnings on height by ethnicity (eth, 4 categories), age category (age, 3) and their cells (eth:age, 12): 13.5_Non-NestedModels.R passes x = height - mean(height) to earnings_latin_square.stan, whose intercepts and slopes per eth, age and eth:age are drawn independently (a1, a2, b1, b2, c, d), so ||; the script's comment states it as lmer with correlated terms. earnings_latin_square.data.json is an identical copy of this table. y is log(earn), x duplicates height and x_centered its centered copy, all ignored. Outside check: the folded copy's model, filed as model 2.
